prompt:
Normalize the one contact block in the user's note. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country; each value is a string or JSON null. No Markdown or prose.

Use only record lines, recognizing label variants, colon/equals/tab separators and any line order. Ignore notes and signatures; never infer fields from email domains, legal suffixes or other clues except for the explicit swap and phone-country rule below. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent, blank or whole-value placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD; case-insensitive) are null except for country as specified below.

Reserve the country line for country. In other lines, route any value containing @ to email; route any value consisting only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / with at least seven digits to phone, testing after stripping leading tel: and a trailing numeric extension of the form ext. N, ext N, xN, #N or extension N. Use the name and company labels for those fields, but swap their values before cleanup if the name value ends in a legal suffix and the company value does not.

Country: map the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, accepting English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes case-insensitively, and common aliases including UK/Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA/U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ.

Phone: after stripping tel: and the extension, a leading + or 00 (ignoring an opening parenthesis) means international. Remove (0) from international numbers, delete spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and convert leading 00 to +. Keep the written calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. If country was absent, blank or a placeholder, fill it from the international calling code only if the code uniquely identifies a country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave it null. For a national phone, remove formatting and one leading trunk 0, if present, then prepend + and the normalized country's calling code; without a country, return null for the phone. Phone strings are E.164 (+ followed by digits only).

Name: reorder Last, First at the first comma; remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof (case-insensitive, optional dot); uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Company: remove a trailing legal suffix and optional preceding comma, trim, and apply the same casing to each space-separated word. Match suffixes case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics through casing; never transliterate. Email: strip surrounding angle brackets and the mailto: prefix, then lowercase the entire address.
